messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy is being steadily eroded by data brokers, biometric scanners, and always-connected devices, yet I judge the prediction to be unlikely because legal frameworks, encryption, and cultural resistance will preserve meaningful boundaries of personal autonomy; Privacy.

Copying a full human consciousness into a computer by the early 2030s is, in my assessment, extraordinarily unlikely because we still lack a coherent theory of how subjective experience maps onto silicon architecture; Copying.

Wireless connectivity will expand dramatically through low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations and next-generation cellular networks, making this prediction quite plausible by the mid-2030s even if every single square meter of terrain proves impractical; Wireless.

All forms of transport becoming fully electric is a reasonable long-term trajectory for personal cars, urban rail, and short-range aviation, yet heavy freight shipping and intercontinental flight face severe battery-energy-density barriers, so I rate it probable but not certain; All.

Irreversibility is, of all these predictions, the most defensible because ice-sheet collapse, ocean thermal inertia, and permafrost methane release operate on century-to-millennium timescales that no present-day policy can undo; Irreversibility.

Physical currency is already being displaced by digital wallets and central-bank digital currencies across most developed economies, so I find this prediction quite likely within two to three decades, though some nations may retain cash for considerably longer; Physical.

Scientists are making genuine advances in senescence biology and gene-editing tools, but the leap from adding a decade of healthy lifespan to enabling centuries or immortality remains so vast that I judge it vanishingly unlikely within any foreseeable timeframe; Scientists.
